## Executive Summary

This document is the technical specification for the IMBUS integrated data product (D2.3,
Type: DATA). It defines the proposed column names, file formats, data tier structure, and
design principles for the standardised representation of the ICES DATRAS bottom trawl survey
exchange tables.

The D2.3 product itself — the parquet files — is hosted at
<https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/> (interim; transfer to the ICES open access portal
is planned under D2.4). Long-term sustainability is handled by WP5: **D5.3** (ICES, M18)
formally integrates the IMBUS data products and the {obus} codebase into the ICES DATRAS R
library and ICES web services. The raw DATRAS data supply that feeds D2.3 is formalised in
**D5.1** (ICES, M6).

The principal design decisions are:

1. **Unified column naming.** A single, consistent set of column names is applied across all
   record types and surveys, regardless of API source or era. The full field mapping is
   documented in [D2.2 §2](D2.2_data_formats_metadata.qmd).
2. **Parquet-based distribution.** HH, HL, and CA exchange tables are stored as columnar
   parquet files enabling fast, column-selective querying without full downloads.
3. **Sentinel value removal.** The DATRAS convention of using −9 for missing values is
   replaced with proper missing-value encoding.
4. **Species resolution via WoRMS AphiaID.** Historical species codes (ITIS TSN, NODC) are
   mapped to current WoRMS AphiaIDs for cross-era joins.
5. **Unique haul identifiers.** An 8-field composite key (`.id`) uniquely identifies each
   haul across all surveys, years, and countries.
6. **A standardised HL product.** A unified standardised representation of the HL exchange
   table — `HL_standardised.parquet` — resolves the unit ambiguities, DataType dependencies,
   and sex-recording heterogeneity of raw HL into a single clean, self-contained product
   covering all valid hauls across all 29 surveys.
7. **DataType-corrected CPUE.** A transparent, reproducible calculation pathway raises raw
   exchange data to catch-per-unit-effort, handling all DataType variants correctly.

The specification is implemented in the R package **{obus}**
(<https://github.com/einarhjorleifsson/obus>). {obus} is explicitly experimental and serves
as the proof-of-concept implementation for the WP2 period; its functionality is intended to
be upstreamed into the official `icesDatras` R package under WP5/D5.3 (M18).

## Background and Purpose {#sec-background}

This document is the technical specification for D2.3, the IMBUS integrated data product.
It should be read alongside **D2.2** (Data Formats and Metadata), which provides the
field-by-field documentation of the current DATRAS exchange format — the reference for the
naming conventions, field descriptions, and known issues that underpin the design decisions
here.

The IMBUS project (Sep 2025 – Aug 2027) is a 24-month EU-funded initiative to improve use
of ICES trawl survey data. WP2 is responsible for data standardisation. The four WP2
objectives are:

1. Assess user requirements. *(Addressed in D2.1, April 2026.)*
2. Develop a data format for WP3–5 products.
3. Generate meta-data descriptions.
4. Process current DATRAS data into the new format.

D2.3 delivers on objectives 2 and 4 — the standardised data product. D2.2 delivers
objective 3 — the metadata documentation.

### Scope

**In scope:**

- Proposed standardised column names and their mapping from current DATRAS names.
- Parquet file format, hosting, and access via the {obus} R package.
- Unique haul identifier (`.id`) construction.
- Design and schema of the standardised HL product (`HL_standardised`).
- Data tier structure (Tier 0 raw / Tier 1 standardised).
- Calculation pathways from raw exchange data to CPUE-by-length and exploratory
  CPUE-by-age.
- {obus} interim status and transition path to `icesDatras` (D5.3).

**Out of scope:**

- Field-by-field documentation of the current DATRAS exchange format — see
  **[D2.2](D2.2_data_formats_metadata.qmd)**.
- Official CPUEA and age-based survey indices (ICES Datacenter products).
- Deployment to the ICES open access portal — subject of **D2.4**.
- Per-survey metadata fact sheets — addressed separately under user requirement UR-Q1.

## IMBUS Proposed Data Formats — D2.3 Product Specification {#sec-imbus}

> **Deliverable D2.3 scope.** This document is the technical specification for the IMBUS
> integrated data product (D2.3, Type: DATA, due M12). It defines the proposed column
> names, file formats, data tier structure, and design principles. The D2.3 product itself —
> the parquet files — will be hosted on the ICES open access portal under D2.4 (M12).
> The current interim location is <https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/>.
>
> Long-term sustainability is handled by WP5: **D5.3** (ICES, M18) formally integrates
> the IMBUS data products and the {obus} codebase into the ICES DATRAS R library and
> ICES web services, ensuring D2.3 has an institutional home beyond the project period.
> The raw DATRAS data supply that feeds D2.3 is formalised in **D5.1** (ICES, M6).

### Standardised Data Formats {#sec-std-formats}

#### Harmonised variables

The IMBUS product uses **standard column names throughout** (see
[D2.2 — Current Issues: column naming](D2.2_data_formats_metadata.qmd#sec-issues)).
Where data originate from the legacy XML API, an automatic translation step maps legacy to
standard names using the field dictionary `dr_lookup_fields`. Fields with no standard
equivalent retain their original names. The full mapping (~292 fields) is available in the
`dr_lookup_fields` data object in {obus} and in the companion
[DATRAS Field Reference](../DATRAS/datras_field_reference_v2.qmd).

> **Interim names.** Two fields — `sex` and `aphia` — use IMBUS canonical names that
> deviate from the (inconsistent) ICES "new" names, as a temporary measure pending
> resolution by the ICES Datacenter. See
> [D2.2 — IMBUS interim canonical names](D2.2_data_formats_metadata.qmd#sec-interim-names).

Additional standardisation steps applied to all exchange tables:

- **Sentinel value removal.** The DATRAS convention of using −9 for missing values is
  replaced with proper missing-value encoding (`NA`).
- **Species resolution.** Historical species codes (ITIS TSN, NODC) are mapped to current
  WoRMS AphiaIDs (`aphia`) for cross-era joins.
- **Unique haul identifier.** An 8-field composite key (`.id`) uniquely identifies each haul
  across all surveys, years, and countries.

#### Unique Haul Identifier {#unique-haul-identifier}

A composite key constructed from eight fields uniquely identifies each haul:

```
.id = Survey : Year : Quarter : Country : Platform : Gear : StationName : HaulNumber
```

Example: `"NS-IBTS:2023:1:NL:58G2:GOV:18:27"`

This is the recommended join key for all operations across the IMBUS product suite. A
shorter 6-field key (omitting `Country` and `StationName`) is also available for comparison
with the ICES CPUEL derived product, which omits those two fields. The 6-field key is
ambiguous — more than 2,400 short keys match more than one haul in the full dataset — and
is provided only for backward-compatibility diagnostics, not for production use.

#### The standardised HL product: design rationale {#sec-standardize-hl}

The raw DATRAS HL exchange table mixes three distinct kinds of information in every row:
length-frequency measurements, haul-level totals, and subsampling metadata. On top of this,
several field values cannot be interpreted without context from other fields or from a
separate table: the length unit depends on a code field (`LengthCode`); the meaning of a
count depends on the haul's `DataType` and `HaulDuration` (both in HH, not HL); and species
are identified by numeric code rather than name. The result is that every analyst must
re-derive units, joins, and scaling from scratch before any analysis can begin.

The IMBUS standardised HL product resolves these ambiguities once, producing a clean,
self-contained table where every column has a single unambiguous meaning. Four design
decisions shape the result.

**Two counting paths, one table.** The HL table contains two independent records of the
same catch: length-frequency measurements (`NumberAtLength`) and haul-level totals
(`TotalNumber`). Both are scaled to consistent units — numbers per haul (`n_haul`) and
numbers per hour of towing (`n_hour`) — and retained in a single table, distinguished by
a `type` column:

- `type = "length"` — counts derived from `NumberAtLength`, one row per species × length
  class per haul. Used for length-structured analyses: length-frequency distributions,
  age-length keys, year-class tracking.
- `type = "haul"` — counts derived from `TotalNumber`, one row per species per haul.
  Used for haul-level totals, biomass indices, and as a cross-check on the length-derived
  totals.

Keeping both paths in a single table, rather than two separate files, means every caught
species is always present (via its `type = "haul"` row) even when it was never individually
measured at length. The `type` flag makes the distinction explicit: any downstream analysis
using `n_haul` or `n_hour` must filter on `type` first.

**Sex as a proportion.** Raw HL records the same haul × species × length class in multiple
rows split by sex. Rather than carrying sex as a row-splitting dimension, the standardised
product collapses sex into a single derived column `p_females` — the proportion of
individually sexed fish at each length class that were female. Female and male counts can
be recovered by multiplying `n_haul` or `n_hour` by `p_females` and `1 − p_females`
respectively. `p_females` is absent when no fish in the group were individually sexed.

**`DevelopmentStage` dropped.** Across the 2010–2020 exchange data, 99.7% of records carry
no developmental stage code; the remainder are summed over during aggregation in any case.
Users who need to work with developmental stage should access the raw HL parquet directly.

**`StandardSpeciesCode` / `BycatchSpeciesCode` not carried through.** These haul-level
flags from HH record what a vessel was obligated to report for each haul. They are not
carried into the standardised product but remain available via a join to HH on `.id`.

#### Summary: proposed data tiers {#sec-tiers}

```
Tier 0 — Raw exchange parquets (hosted)
  HH.parquet, HL.parquet, CA.parquet, LT.parquet
  All original submission fields; standard names applied on fetch; −9 → NA.
  For: expert users, QC, full-fidelity reproduction.

Tier 1 — Standardised HL product (hosted)
  HL_standardised.parquet   Unified type="length" + type="haul" rows; valid hauls only.
                            Generated by: dr_HL_standardised(dr_con("HH"), dr_con("HL"),
                                                             haulval = "V")
                            Accessed via: dr_con("HL_standardised")
  For: all survey-analysis users; the recommended starting point for CPUE, indices,
       length distributions, and biomass workflows.

Official ICES derived products (accessible via dr_get())
  CPUEA / IDX   Age-based CPUE and indices; ICES Datacenter products.
  For: formal stock assessment; not produced by IMBUS.
```

### File Formats Used {#sec-file-formats}

#### Parquet

The IMBUS product distributes HH, HL, CA, and the standardised HL as columnar **parquet**
files. Parquet enables fast, column-selective querying without downloading the full table —
a critical advantage given that HL alone contains tens of millions of rows across all
surveys and years.

| Table | URL |
|-------|-----|
| HH | `https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/HH.parquet` |
| HL | `https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/HL.parquet` |
| CA | `https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/CA.parquet` |
| HL_standardised | `https://heima.hafro.is/~einarhj/datras/HL_standardised.parquet` |

These files are readable by any tool that supports the parquet format or the DuckDB query
engine: R, Python, Julia, DBeaver, and others.

#### Data access via {obus}

The {obus} R package provides two access modes:

**Lazy parquet connection (recommended for large queries).** A connection to a parquet file
returns a lazy query object. Filters are pushed down to the file; only the requested rows
and columns are transferred into memory:

```r
library(obus)
library(dplyr)

# Length-frequency CPUE — filter to length rows and desired species/survey
cod_lengths <- dr_con("HL_standardised") |>
  filter(type == "length", Survey == "NS-IBTS", latin == "Gadus morhua") |>
  collect()

# Haul-level catch totals
cod_hauls <- dr_con("HL_standardised") |>
  filter(type == "haul", Survey == "NS-IBTS", latin == "Gadus morhua") |>
  collect()
```

**Full download via `dr_get()`.** Downloads and collects an entire table into memory,
optionally filtered via the legacy ICES XML API. Appropriate for smaller, targeted queries.

#### {obus}: interim status and transition path {#sec-obus-status}

{obus} is **explicitly experimental** (lifecycle status: experimental) and is best understood
as the proof-of-concept implementation for the WP2 data standardisation work. It is not
intended to be a permanent, standalone R package. Its role within the IMBUS project lifecycle
is:

1. **Proof-of-concept.** Provide a working, validated implementation of the naming
   conventions, DataType arithmetic, parquet access, and CPUE pathways described in this
   document during the WP2 delivery period (M1–M12).
2. **D2.3 delivery vehicle.** Serve as the primary means of accessing the D2.3 data product
   (parquet files) while those files are hosted on the interim server.
3. **Design feedback loop.** Accumulate community experience and feedback that directly
   informs what is worth upstreaming into the official ICES infrastructure.

{obus} **builds on, rather than replaces**, the official `icesDatras` package — it imports
`icesDatras` and delegates XML-source downloads to it. The added value is the
parquet/DuckDB access layer, unified column naming, DataType-aware derived fields, and the
quality-check family.

**Intended trajectory.** Under WP5/D5.3 (ICES, M18), the functionality proven in {obus} is
a candidate for integration into the official ICES DATRAS R library (`icesDatras`), alongside
migration of the parquet files to ICES-managed infrastructure. The naming-convention mapping,
the DataType arithmetic, and the composite haul key (`.id`) are the most transferable
elements.

### Updated Meta-data Descriptions {#sec-updated-metadata}

The IMBUS standard names and field definitions described in D2.2 §2 and this document
constitute an updated meta-data description for the DATRAS exchange tables. The companion
document [DATRAS Field Reference](../DATRAS/datras_field_reference_v2.qmd) provides complete field
reference tables for all HH, HL, CA, and LT fields, including types, units, valid values,
and a drop-or-derive quick reference.

Per-survey meta-data fact sheets (coverage, gear history, time-series breaks, QC history) are
not produced by D2.3. These are addressed separately under user requirement UR-Q1.

### Standardised Code for Processing DATRAS Data {#sec-code}

WP2 does not generate new CPUE data series. Instead, it provides transparent, reproducible
code that any user can apply to the standardised exchange tables to generate CPUE on demand.

#### Data flow

```
DATRAS database
      │
      ▼
Raw exchange download    ← getDATRAS() (legacy XML API)
      │
      ▼
Type normalisation       ← dr_settypes(): column types enforced; −9 → NA
Column renaming          ← dr_translate(): legacy → standard names
      │
      ▼
Raw parquets (server)    ← HH.parquet / HL.parquet / CA.parquet
      │
      ▼
Standardised HL          ← dr_HL_standardised(dr_con("HH"), dr_con("HL"), haulval="V")
  (server)               ← HL_standardised.parquet
      │
      ▼
User analysis            ← dr_con("HL_standardised") |> filter(type == ...) |> collect()
                         → dr_catch_by_haul() / dr_expand_length() for zero-filling
```

Stages 1–3 are handled once by the data provider (currently Einar Hjörleifsson; ICES from
D2.4/D5.3). The standardised HL is regenerated whenever the raw parquets are updated.
Users interact from stage 4 onward.

#### {obus} helper functions

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `dr_add_id()` | Construct the 8-field composite haul key `.id` |
| `dr_add_length_cm()` | Standardise `LengthClass` to centimetres, accounting for `LengthCode` |
| `dr_add_length_mm()` | Standardise `LengthClass` to millimetres |
| `dr_add_n_and_cpue()` | Compute DataType-corrected `n_haul` and `n_hour` from `NumberAtLength` |
| `dr_HL_standardised()` | Build the standardised HL table on demand from raw HH + HL |
| `dr_catch_by_haul()` | Zero-filled haul totals from the standardised HL |
| `dr_expand_length()` | Zero-filled complete length grid from the standardised HL |
| `dr_check_*()` | Quality-check family; returns a report tibble without throwing errors |
| `dr_get_areas()` | Survey strata as a spatial object |
| `dr_assign_area()` | Spatial join of haul positions to survey strata |

#### CPUE calculation pathway

**CPUE-by-length** requires five steps:

1. **Filter valid hauls:** retain only hauls with `HaulValidity = "V"`. *(Pre-applied in `HL_standardised`.)*
2. **Filter standard species records:** retain `SpeciesValidity = "1"`.
3. **Join `DataType` and `HaulDuration` from HH to HL** on `.id`. *(Pre-applied.)*
4. **Compute `n_haul` and `n_hour`** using the DataType-appropriate formula. *(Pre-applied.)*
5. **Aggregate** across sex and species category. *(Pre-applied; sex summarised as `p_females`.)*

For users working from `dr_con("HL_standardised")`, steps 1, 3, 4, and 5 are already
complete. The remaining user step is to filter `SpeciesValidity = "1"` and select the
survey, species, and year range of interest.

The DataType-aware arithmetic that underpins step 4 handles the three submission conventions:

| DataType | Meaning | `n_haul` | `n_hour` |
|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| R (raw) | Sorted, possibly sub-sampled | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` (NA → 1) | `n_haul × 60 / HaulDuration` |
| S, P (bulk / size-stratified) | Sub-sampled; SubsamplingFactor always > 1 | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` | `n_haul × 60 / HaulDuration` |
| C (CPUE already) | Pre-raised to 1-hour equivalent | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor × HaulDuration / 60` | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` |

`HaulDuration` is in minutes throughout. CPUE = catch in numbers per one hour of towing.

#### Zero observations and zero-fill

A CPUE value of zero means the species was **absent** from that haul but was caught by at
least one vessel in the same survey × year × quarter. Zero rows are required for unbiased
abundance indices: when aggregating CPUE across hauls within a stratum, hauls where the
species was not observed must contribute a zero — omitting them inflates the mean.

`HL_standardised` contains only observed rows (no zeros). Zero-filling is applied downstream
by `dr_catch_by_haul()` and `dr_expand_length()`, which add an explicit zero row for every
haul in a `Survey × Year × Quarter` where a given species was absent. This matches the
convention used by the official ICES CPUE data products.

**A note on phantom zeros.** The pooled zero-fill approach can produce phantom zeros for
hauls that were never required to record a given species. The DATRAS HH table records what
each vessel was obligated to report (`StandardSpeciesCode`, `BycatchSpeciesCode`), and the
official ICES index methodology uses these flags for a further haul-selection step. The
{obus} zero-fill functions follow the DATRAS CPUE product convention and do not implement
this additional filter. Users building formal survey indices should apply haul-selection
using the HH flags directly.

### The `HL_standardised` product {#sec-hl-standardised}

`HL_standardised.parquet` is the delivered Tier 1 standardised HL product. It covers
**all 29 DATRAS surveys**, valid hauls only, and is derived directly from the raw HH and HL
parquets by `dr_HL_standardised(dr_con("HH"), dr_con("HL"), haulval = "V")`. It is
accessible via `dr_con("HL_standardised")`.

**Schema:**

| Column | Type | Unit | Notes |
|--------|------|------|-------|
| `.id` | chr | — | 8-field composite haul key |
| `Survey` | chr | — | Survey acronym |
| `Year` | int | — | Survey year |
| `Quarter` | int | — | Survey quarter |
| `aphia` | int | — | Resolved WoRMS AphiaID |
| `latin` | chr | — | WoRMS accepted Latin name |
| `species` | chr | — | Common (vernacular) name |
| `type` | chr | — | `"length"` or `"haul"` (see design rationale) |
| `length_mm` | dbl | mm | Standardised length in mm; `NA` for `type = "haul"` rows |
| `length_cm` | dbl | cm | Standardised length in cm; `NA` for `type = "haul"` rows |
| `accuracy` | dbl | cm | Length measurement resolution; `NA` for `type = "haul"` rows |
| `n_haul` | dbl | count | DataType-corrected numbers per haul |
| `n_hour` | dbl | count/hr | DataType-corrected numbers per hour of towing |
| `w_haul` | dbl | g | Catch weight per haul; `NA` for `type = "length"` rows and when weight not recorded |
| `w_hour` | dbl | g/hr | Catch weight per hour; `NA` as for `w_haul` |
| `p_females` | dbl | proportion | Fraction of sexed individuals that are female; `NA` when no sexing data |
| `SpeciesValidity` | chr | — | Record type code — **filter to `"1"` before analysis** |

**Key derivation decisions:**

- **Valid hauls only.** HL is joined to HH records where `HaulValidity = "V"`. Invalid
  hauls are excluded.
- **Length records only in `type = "length"` rows.** Rows where `LengthClass` is absent
  (totals-only and presence/absence record types) are excluded from `type = "length"` rows.
- **`SpeciesValidity` retained (interim).** No filter on `SpeciesValidity` is applied
  during product derivation; it is retained so that records of different types co-occur
  visibly. For most analyses, filter to `SpeciesValidity = "1"` after collecting. The
  correct handling of non-`"1"` codes is an open question pending clarification from the
  ICES Datacenter.
- **No zero-fill.** The product contains observed rows only. Zero-filling is applied by the
  user downstream via `dr_catch_by_haul()` or `dr_expand_length()` as needed.

**Comparison with the ICES CPUEL product** (for length-frequency CPUE):

| | ICES CPUEL | `HL_standardised` (type = "length") |
|-|-----------|--------------------------------------|
| Surveys covered | 8 | All 29 |
| Haul validity filter | None applied | Valid hauls only |
| Haul key | 6 fields (2,400+ ambiguous) | Full `.id` (8 fields; unambiguous) |
| `SpeciesValidity` filter | Pre-filtered to `"1"` | Retained — user filters after collecting |
| Sex retained | NA for 7 of 8 surveys | Collapsed to `p_females` |
| Weight | Not included | `w_hour` available from `type = "haul"` rows |
| Species identifier | Scientific name string | Latin name + common name + AphiaID |
| Zero-catch hauls | Present (added by DATRAS) | Not included — add downstream |

See [DATRAS/cpue_derivation.qmd](../DATRAS/cpue_derivation.qmd) for a detailed
comparison of the two approaches.

---

### Exploratory CPUE-by-age {#cpue-by-age}

Age-disaggregated CPUE is achievable from the exchange tables but involves analytical choices
that the IMBUS standardisation does not prescribe:

| | Official CPUEA | Exploratory CPUE-by-age |
|-|---------------|------------------------|
| ALK source | ICES expert-group agreed | User-defined from CA |
| Pooling level | Survey/species specific | User's choice |
| Plus-group handling | Agreed convention | User's choice |
| Appropriate for | Formal stock assessment | Research, exploration |
| Accessible via | `dr_get("CPUEA", ...)` | User pipeline on HL_standardised + CA |

The general pathway: (1) use `HL_standardised` filtered to `type = "length"` as the
CPUE-by-length input; (2) construct an age-length key from CA; (3) apply the ALK to the
length CPUE; (4) aggregate across hauls. Step 1 is directly satisfied by
`dr_con("HL_standardised")`, substantially reducing the entry barrier for this approach.

A pre-computed `CA_raised.parquet` product (one row per `.id × aphia × age`) has been
proposed as a complement to `HL_standardised`. Its design requires input from WP4 on ALK
pooling level, plus-group threshold, and area-pooled CA rows; see
[Appendix 2](#sec-appendix2-hl-proposals) for the current schema sketch.

## Discussion and Conclusions {#sec-discussion}

The D2.3 product specification addresses a long-standing barrier to broader use of ICES
bottom trawl survey data: the complexity of deriving analysis-ready products from the raw
DATRAS exchange format. The raw format is rich and flexible — necessarily so, to accommodate
the diversity of national sampling protocols across 29 surveys — but that same flexibility
imposes a substantial entry cost on users who simply want species-level catch-per-unit-effort
for a given survey and year. Every analyst has historically had to resolve unit ambiguities,
handle DataType-conditional arithmetic, and manage zero-filling independently, with no
assurance of consistency across research groups.

**A single standardised product for the majority of use cases.** The `HL_standardised`
parquet delivers what most users need in one file: DataType-corrected counts at length and
at the haul level, species names resolved, lengths in a single consistent unit, and sex
summarised in a recoverable form. The `type` column cleanly separates the two counting paths
that raw HL conflates, so users working with length distributions filter to
`type = "length"`, while users working with haul totals or biomass filter to
`type = "haul"` — without needing to understand the underlying DataType conventions or
subsampling arithmetic.

**Coverage and quality are substantially improved relative to the ICES CPUEL product.**
The official CPUEL product covers 8 of 29 surveys and does not apply a haul-validity filter.
`HL_standardised` covers all 29 surveys, filters to valid hauls, and provides an unambiguous
8-field join key. For the 8 surveys where CPUEL exists, WP2's analysis confirmed that the
`HL_standardised` CPUE series are consistent with CPUEL (modulo the known structural
differences), validating the derivation.

**The design makes an implicit contract explicit.** The raw HL table contains two
independent records of the same catch — length-frequency measurements and haul-level totals
— mixed in the same rows without any formal distinction. The standardised product separates
these into two row types with consistent column names and units. When the two paths agree,
users can proceed with confidence; a persistent divergence points to a genuine data
inconsistency in the original submission, flagged by the `dr_check_totalno()` quality
function.

**Known limitations.** Three open items require acknowledgement. First, the zero-fill
convention — pooling species across all hauls in a survey × year × quarter — matches the
DATRAS CPUE product convention but can produce phantom zeros for hauls never required to
record a given species. Formal index calculations should apply the additional haul-selection
step using the `StandardSpeciesCode` and `BycatchSpeciesCode` flags in HH. Second, the
pre-computed `CA_raised` product (age-disaggregated abundance) has not been produced; its
design depends on WP4 input on ALK pooling conventions that has not yet been finalised.
Third, the parquet files remain on an interim personal server; transfer to ICES-managed
infrastructure is pending D2.4 and D5.3.

**Sustainability and reproducibility.** `HL_standardised` is derived from the raw exchange
parquets using a single documented function call (`dr_HL_standardised()`). Any user can
reproduce the product from the Tier 0 parquets using open code, without any intermediate
files. The {obus} package is explicitly experimental; its functionality, together with the
parquet files, is a candidate for integration into the official `icesDatras` R package and
ICES-managed infrastructure under WP5/D5.3 (M18). At that point the D2.3 products will have
an institutional home within ICES that ensures their long-term availability and maintenance.

---

## Further Work {#sec-further-work}

The following items are open as of the date of this document:

1. **Parquet hosting.** The current parquet files are on a personal server
   (`heima.hafro.is`). Transfer to the ICES open access portal is pending WP5/ICES
   coordination (D2.4).

2. **Integration into ICES infrastructure (D5.3).** Per decisions from the 1 June 2026
   IMBUS WP2-WP5 meeting, parquet/DuckDB functionality should be incorporated into the
   official ICES DATRAS R package rather than maintained as a separate tool. This is
   formally the scope of WP5 deliverable D5.3 (ICES, M18).

3. **`CA_raised` product.** Age-disaggregated abundance (one row per `.id × aphia × age`)
   derived from ALK application to `HL_standardised`. Design requires input from WP4 on ALK
   pooling level, plus-group threshold, and area-pooled CA rows. See
   [Appendix 2](#sec-appendix2-hl-proposals) for the current schema sketch.

4. **Haul-selection step for formal indices.** The phantom-zero limitation described in
   §[Standardised Code for Processing DATRAS Data](#sec-code) requires implementing a
   haul-selection filter using `StandardSpeciesCode` / `BycatchSpeciesCode`. This is needed
   before `HL_standardised` can serve as a drop-in input for formal survey index
   calculation.

5. **Area standardisation.** Mapping from haul positions to C-squares and ICES statistical
   divisions is partially implemented (`dr_assign_area()`) but the lookup helpers are not
   yet complete in {obus}.

## Appendix 2 — Superseded and Pending Intermediate Proposals {#sec-appendix2-hl-proposals}

### `CA_raised.parquet` (design pending)

One row per `.id × aphia × age`. Age-disaggregated abundance from ALK application to
`HL_standardised`. Design requires input from WP4 on ALK pooling level, plus-group
threshold, and area-pooled CA rows. Proposed schema:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `.id` | chr | Haul join key |
| `aphia` | int | Resolved WoRMS AphiaID |
| `age` | int | Age class (years) |
| `plus_group` | lgl | Whether this represents the open-ended plus group |
| `n_haul` | dbl | Estimated numbers at age per haul (ALK × HL catch) |
| `n_hour` | dbl | Numbers at age per hour |
| `alk_source` | chr | Pooling level used to construct the ALK |
